_comment: Where this template's mechanisms came FROM, and how far each source has been read. Written by hand, read by bin/skeletor-maintain, never merged from. skeletor was extracted from a mature production repository and that repository kept going; this is the record of how far along it we have looked. An upstream is located by its origin URL, never by a path — a path is right on one machine and wrong on every other.

jam-sense.why: the repository every mechanism in this template was extracted from

sources.cli/task.py: the second capture intake, and the argument for two lanes over a --kind flag
sources.scripts/reporting/remediation.py: the Capture descriptor: one engine, N lanes, and drainer_line deriving a schedule from the job registry rather than storing it
sources.scripts/reporting/bug_capture.py: the shared capture engine this template's cli/_capture.py is a smaller version of
sources.tests/test_pyright_scope.py: the caller scan: config pins OR every caller passes --pythonpath. Merged to develop as 8835dff73 (PR #1423), which the watermark above now sits on. It is also the one file here whose direction has reversed: jam-sense took it FROM this template at v0.4.2 (their .skeletor-components.json records it at the path it had then, template/python/tests/test_pyright_scope.py), added the interpreter half, and it came back. Expect it to keep moving in both directions rather than reading either way as drift.

sources_untracked._comment: Harvested from, and NOT trackable. These paths are gitignored upstream, so they have no history for a watermark to measure against and this report can never say whether they moved. Recorded as a limit rather than rediscovered as an error on every run — and kept out of `sources`, because a path git cannot see is not the same fact as one that has left the tree.
sources_untracked..vscode/settings.json: the issue and pull-request query grouping — the read side of the capture lanes. jam-sense's .gitignore:52 ignores .vscode/, so their queries live on one machine and are not shared or backed up. Ours are generated from scripts/lanes.py and tracked, which is the difference that made the port worth doing rather than copying.

_not_taken._comment: Judged and declined, with the reason, so the next pass does not re-litigate it. An entry here is a decision; delete it if the reason stops holding rather than silently harvesting anyway.

jam-sense.scripts/reporting/remediation.py (the dr: 2501 lines of Kuma monitors, an escalation policy and a run ledger. The template ships ONE fully-worked job on purpose — a registry seeded with keys whose modules do not exist is red on arrival — so the drain side stays the adopter's. The capture side ported; the drain side is named by scripts/lanes.py and left to them.
jam-sense.scripts/reporting/agent_test_gap.py: a lane with no producer in this template. A view whose label nothing can create is empty forever, and an empty pane and a drained queue render identically.
jam-sense.the editor fallback on a capture (jam ta: worth having and not yet ported. It needs a body template per lane, which is a second copy of Lane.sections unless it is generated from them.
jam-sense.the agent-fix / agent-fix-excluded parki: labels nothing in this template applies. Same rule as the test-gap lane: a lane needs a producer, and a view whose label nothing can create is empty forever — indistinguishable from a queue you have kept clear.
jam-sense.a gate asserting the pinned virtualenv E: Correct and unassertable from a unit test. `venvPath` is relative to the config file, so it names the checkout: the pin falls through in a linked worktree, and jam-sense measured it falling through in four checkouts of five. Reproduced here — 0 errors in a scaffold's primary and 27 in a fresh worktree of the same commit. The honest assertion is checkout-dependent: red in CI, which passes --pythonpath instead, and red in every unprovisioned worktree. Written into pyrightconfig.json as a limit beside the pin, and closed for the case this template creates by having `worktree new` link a .venv.
